clue.text: French stocking one's found in Spain

definitions.meaning: a close-fitting bodice of French name, worn with suspenders to hold up stockings; bas is also French for stocking
a native of the region straddling the western Pyrenees, much of it in northern Spain

explanation.surface: A French woman's hosiery turns up in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is loose: the garment is a lingerie bodice that often holds up stockings, and bas is the French word for stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice-style item of lingerie, and a member of the people of the Pyrenees region partly in Spain.

clue.text: Waving torch is hot

parts.note: a brand is a burning stick or torch
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Someone waves a hot torch around.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a weapon or object is to wave it about, often in threat or display.

clue.text: In the main a tide is turning for member of the Rose family

indicators.note: the turned letters are placed in the main, which wraps them

parts.note: the main is an old poetic term for the sea

indicators.note: turning says the a and the tide are read backwards

parts.note: a rip is a rough stretch of water, as in rip tide

explanation.surface: At sea, a tide turns for a rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes PIRA; 'the main' is the poetic name for the open sea, not 'chiefly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering shrub genus related to roses, often called meadowsweet or bridal wreath.

clue.text: Raise sweet head, timeless, without braids

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it from the bottom up

parts.note: a dessert is a sweet course

indicators.note: timeless means the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Raise your sweet head, losing track of time, with your hair loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' drops T from NUT for NU; 'Raise' turns DESSERT plus NU upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresses are long locks or plaits, so having none of them means unbraided hair.

clue.text: Note team in gold is one with little chance of winning

definitions.text: one with little chance of winning

indicators.note: the note and team sit in the word for gold, so it encloses them

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
UT is the old name for the first note of the scale, later doh
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A musical note, a team and gold suggest a sporting final with an underdog.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the old name for the note now called doh. OR is heraldry's gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner or competitor thought unlikely to win is described with this term in racing and politics.

clue.text: Lingerie nobleman unties perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A nobleman unties some lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: A coy, humorous term for underwear, things too delicate to be spoken of.

clue.text: Settled with your Greek god

parts.note: sat means settled or perched

explanation.surface: Your Greek god has settled down.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland deity of Greek myth, part man and part goat, attending Dionysus.

clue.text: Father aims to change movement

parts.note: dad is a word for father

indicators.note: to change says these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A father plans to change direction.
explanation.definitionFit: An early twentieth-century anti-art movement in Europe that mocked convention.

clue.text: Take endless song and put in the short beat

indicators.note: the shortened article goes inside the shortened song
endless means the song loses its last letter

parts.note: a rhyme can be a song or jingle

indicators.note: short means the article loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Take a song and put a short beat into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' gives RHYM and 'short' gives TH; 'Take' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular pulse in music or speech is its pattern of beats.

clue.text: Here one's suffering from a disturbance of the mind that's ominous

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's stands for is and joins on

parts.words: suffering from a disturbance of the mind
parts.note: mental, informally, means mentally disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone present suffers a disturbing state of mind that feels threatening.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a foreboding of something about to happen, so threatening or full of foreboding.

clue.text: Temporarily, racket can be seen by terrace in market

indicators.note: racket and terrace are set in the market, which wraps round them

parts.note: AIM is the Alternative Investment Market of the London Stock Exchange
a din is a loud racket
TER is a short form of terrace in addresses

explanation.surface: Noise from a terrace carries across a busy market for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: AIM is the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase meaning for the meantime, used of provisional arrangements.

clue.text: Bear this boy's trouble

definitions.meaning: a soft toy bear, named after President Roosevelt
put before boy, the word gives the 1950s British youth in Edwardian dress, seen as a troublemaker

explanation.surface: A young lad's cuddly bear is causing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits with a reputation for rowdiness. The word is also a one-piece undergarment, fitting the lingerie theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuddly toy bear, and the first half of the phrase for a rowdy 1950s youth.

clue.text: Storage for artists

definitions.meaning: sliding boxes in a chest for keeping things

explanation.definitionFit: Sliding compartments in furniture store things, and people who sketch are those who draw.

clue.text: Women's Institute standing in front of church and not before cathedral

indicators.note: the word for and not comes first, ahead of the institute
the institute's letters come ahead of the church's

parts.note: nor means and not
WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

explanation.surface: The Women's Institute stands outside a church but not by a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a long-standing British women's community organisation, abbreviated WI.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Anglian city has a famous Norman cathedral, so the city is named by its cathedral.

clue.text: Remains of ropes

definitions.meaning: on a ship, the ropes supporting a mast

explanation.definitionFit: To linger is a verb sense, and ropes bracing a ship's mast share the same word; it is also a corset.

clue.text: Catch and book gang returning for explosive device

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them

indicators.note: returning says book and gang are read backwards together

parts.note: a mob is a gang

explanation.surface: Police catch a gang and charge them over a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns B plus MOB round to give BOMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A home-made explosive packed with nails as shrapnel, a terrorist weapon.

clue.text: Support one moving towards front in bar serving food

indicators.note: the letter for one shifts nearer the start of the word

parts.note: a brasserie is a bar that serves food
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone works their way to the front of a busy restaurant bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving towards front' moves the I in BRASSERIE two places forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra is an undergarment that gives the bust support.

clue.text: Garment seen in river I fish

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Someone fishing in the river sees a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless undergarment for the upper body is an item of clothing.

clue.text: At first George and Henry (a Scot) could be non-violent

indicators.note: only the opening letter of George is wanted

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: George and Henry, with a Scottish friend, might be peaceful people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Following the peaceful-resistance philosophy of the Indian leader Mahatma, who championed passive protest.

clue.text: A speed in a car or a vessel

parts.note: speed on a car's dial is measured in mph, miles per hour

explanation.surface: A speeding car or boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient two-handled jar for wine or oil is a vessel for holding liquid.

clue.text: Service for women once each is bewildered

parts.note: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army branch in the Second World War

explanation.surface: Every member of a former women's service is confused.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS was the women's branch of the British Army in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be lost or confused, as if adrift on the ocean.

clue.text: Cheers for favoured among list of candidates

indicators.note: the word for favoured goes among the candidates' list, inside it

parts.note: a slate is a list of candidates for election
in means favoured, in fashion

explanation.surface: An election crowd cheers the favourite on the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is the drinking toast, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gaelic drinking toast wishing good health, raised as glasses clink.

clue.text: Instructions to put a bit of flavour in cheeses

indicators.note: the bit of flavour goes inside the cheeses

parts.note: brie is a French soft cheese

indicators.note: only the opening letter of flavour is used

explanation.surface: A recipe says to add a little flavour to cheeses.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer's or agent's instructions for a task, the briefing for a job.

clue.text: Reply in chambers during ceremony

indicators.note: the chambers come during the ceremony, splitting it

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
pos are chamber pots, po being the colloquial British word

explanation.surface: Someone answers back in court chambers in the middle of a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chambers' misleads towards a judge's rooms; it means chamber pots, POS.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, witty retort is a reply in conversation, and also a fencing counter-thrust.

clue.text: Cook fish ahead of time for group of workers

indicators.note: cook in the sense of tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cook the fish in advance for the workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of workers on duty together at one stretch of time, like a night crew.

clue.text: Fragrant foodstuff (ground mast) found in half of Mumbai

indicators.note: the ground letters are placed inside the half of the city name
the second half of the city name is taken
ground means crushed and reworked, so the letters of mast are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fragrant food made from ground mast turns up in Mumbai.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' gives ASMAT; 'half of' takes the second half of the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-grain aromatic rice from the Indian subcontinent, valued for its scent.

clue.text: Priest holds company to be cause of food poisoning

indicators.note: the priest holds the company within him

parts.note: Eli was the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest keeps company that leads to food poisoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A gut bacterium whose harmful strains cause serious food poisoning.

clue.text: In addition, the soldiers and peacekeepers will get taken out initially

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: only the opening letters of taken and out are wanted

explanation.surface: Soldiers and peacekeepers will be taken out first.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning besides or to that, used for something added.

clue.text: Isn't 'lacy' coded for 'with barely enough coverage'?

indicators.note: coded means put into cipher, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Is a lacy garment a coded way of saying it hardly covers anything?
explanation.definitionFit: Barely, skimpily dressed; scant cover means insufficient amount of clothing.

clue.text: Photographic fault coming from overnight flight

definitions.meaning: the glowing pupils caused by flash in pictures
a night plane journey that leaves passengers bleary

explanation.surface: A camera flaw caused by taking a night flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Flash photos give pupils a glow, and a night flight leaves travellers' eyes bloodshot.
